sections.h2: Who sells houses in Calumet City, and how?
sections.html:
Sellers in Calumet City include longtime owners, landlords, heirs and people holding houses that sat empty. The 2020 census found about one in ten housing units vacant, and QuickFacts shows owners living in 55.7 percent of units, a lower share than in most nearby suburbs.

That mix produces three common routes: a listing handled by an agent, a sale you manage yourself, and a direct sale to a cash buyer who accepts repairs and tenants as they come. A listing suits an updated house, and a cash buyer suits a house a lender would balk at. Each route needs the city's transfer stamp and a paid final water bill, and the sections below walk through both in order, starting with what the stamp costs.

sections.h2: How did Calumet City get its name and its layout?
sections.html:
"Cal City," as locals say, lies in Cook County's Thornton Township right on the Indiana line, covering 7.32 square miles. Hammond borders it on the east, Burnham and Chicago on the north, Lansing on the south and South Holland and Dolton on the west.

Schrumville and Sobieski Park merged in 1893 as West Hammond. During Prohibition in Indiana the town drew drinkers across the line and earned the nickname "Sin City." Voters switched to the Calumet City name in 1923, and demolition of the bars along the old "Sin Strip" began in 1995. Two water towers painted with smiley faces, one near River Oaks Mall and one on State Street by Interstate 94, are local landmarks.

The 2020 count was 36,033 residents. The 2025 estimate is 34,798, which is 3.5 percent below the 2020 base.

sections.h2: What does QuickFacts say about home values in Calumet City?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts a typical Calumet City home at $145,200 for 2020 through 2024, and the typical gross rent at $1,177. Middle-point household income is $55,369, and 23.4 percent of residents live below the poverty line.

sections.h2: What does the Calumet City transfer stamp cost?
sections.html:
The clerk's Real Estate Transfer Declaration prints $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof for the buyer and the same for the seller, which totals $8.00 per $1,000 or part thereof. The form is written for transfers up to and including $2 million.

  • Collect the stamps at least 48 hours ahead and leave about half an hour for processing.
  • Only certified checks, money orders or cash are taken.
  • Whoever requests the stamp must be the owner of record, an attorney or a broker, and an agent writes a bar or license number on the form.
  • An exempt transfer cites a paragraph of Sec. 82-323 of the municipal code and submits a copy of the deed.

The City Clerk's office answers at (708) 891-8110, Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The form lists Thornton Township and ZIP code 60409 for the property.

sections.h2: How is the final water bill handled in Calumet City?
sections.html:
Every outstanding water bill has to be paid before a property is sold, and the seller or the seller's representative orders a final meter reading at least 48 hours before the stamp is bought. Call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121 to schedule it.

The city's Water Service Information page prints these monthly rates under Utilities Ordinance 26-01, and warns that water rates move automatically with any increase from Chicago or Hammond:

  • Water, $11.45 per 1,000 gallons.
  • Sewer, $1.33 per 1,000 gallons.
  • Stormwater, $2.00 per 1,000 gallons or part thereof.
  • Refuse, $31.30 per unit, with a $15.65 rate for a first unit at age 65.

The water comes entirely from Lake Michigan, per the city. A new owner files a water service application, and some accounts require a deposit.

sections.h2: What do rental and vacancy rules mean for a Calumet City seller?
sections.html:
The city's Forms & Applications page lists a rental application, an annual rental code compliance letter, an owner-occupied form, a Crime Free Housing licensing application and a vacant and foreclosed property registration. A landlord selling a rental should confirm that the application and the compliance letter are current, because a buyer's attorney tends to ask for them.

Ask Building & Zoning, (708) 891-8120, whether the vacant and foreclosed registration applies to your house and whether any permit or violation is open on the address. The same page offers permit forms for building, electrical, plumbing, HVAC and fences, and an overhead sewer rebate program form. A quick call before accepting an offer avoids surprises after the inspection.

sections.h2: What did the 2020 census count for Calumet City's housing?
sections.html:
Wikipedia's summary of the 2020 census lists 16,196 housing units in Calumet City and 14,549 households, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 3.7 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 8.4 percent. The median age was 39.1, and about 36 percent of households were one person living alone.

The higher vacancy figures matter to a seller, since a house competes with empty units on the same blocks. Pricing against recent closed sales within a few blocks, rather than against a metro-wide number, gives a more honest picture, and a clean, inspected house stands out most in that kind of market.

sections.h2: Where is a Calumet City deed recorded?
sections.html:
Cook County's Clerk runs the Recordings Division, which keeps office hours from 9 to 5 and accepts its last customer at 4:45. Buyer and seller also complete the PTAX-203 Illinois declaration.

The state levies its own tax of 50 cents per $500, and the Department of Revenue notes that home rule municipalities may add theirs, the category Calumet City's stamp falls into. For the property tax proration, the Assessor says exemptions appear as deductions on the second installment bill, so ask the County Treasurer for the amounts and due dates on your parcel.

sections.h2: Whom should a Calumet City seller call first?
sections.html:
Calumet City sits beside Hammond, Lansing, Dolton and South Holland, so buyers often compare it with houses across several municipal lines. A listing should state commute and highway access, since the average trip to work runs 34.4 minutes.

Three city numbers cover most of a handover: the clerk at (708) 891-8110, Water Billing at (708) 891-8121 and Public Works at (708) 891-8161. A cash buyer comfortable with tenants in place, an older furnace or an overhead sewer can often close faster than a buyer who needs a loan, while a retail buyer pays more for a house that has been updated.

faqs.q: What is the Calumet City transfer stamp price?
faqs.a: The clerk's form lists $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof for the buyer and $4.00 for the seller, $8.00 in total per $1,000 or part thereof, for transfers up to and including $2 million.

faqs.q: How is a final water reading ordered in Calumet City?
faqs.a: Call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121. The city asks for the order at least 48 hours before the stamp is bought, and all water bills must be paid before the sale.

faqs.q: What payment does the stamp office accept?
faqs.a: Certified check, money order or cash only, according to the declaration form. Plan to pick the stamps up at least 48 hours ahead.

faqs.q: Which office records a Calumet City deed?
faqs.a: The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, because the city is in Cook County. It takes customers until 4:45 p.m.

faqs.q: Can a rental house in Calumet City be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The city has a rental application and an annual compliance letter, so confirm both are in order and ask Building & Zoning at (708) 891-8120 about open permits before signing a contract.
